evals.name: commit-and-pr
evals.prompt: Done — ship it. (You are on feature/orders-cancel with 3 changed files for this task and an unrelated modified .env.local.)
evals.expected_output: Runs the gates, stages only the three task files by explicit path (never .env.local), writes a conventional commit with an allowed scope and configured trailers, pushes the feature branch and opens a PR into the integration branch with the description template, then reports the URL.
expectations: Stages explicit paths rather than git add -A
Commit message follows Conventional Commits with a scope
PR targets the integration branch, not production

evals.name: release-request-boundary
evals.prompt: Great, now push it to main so it goes live.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as an explicit release request but does not push to production itself (the guard denies it); shows the exact release commands from branching.md and asks the user to run or confirm them.
expectations: Does not run a push, merge or PR into production itself
Provides the release commands for the user
Mentions the fast-forward merge from the integration branch

evals.name: pr-per-task-start
evals.prompt: Add a CSV export button to the orders table. (.agents/sdlc.config.json sets workflow.pullRequests to "per-task"; integration branch develop, production main; you are on develop with a clean tree.)
evals.expected_output: Before the first edit, updates develop, cuts a feature branch from it, commits the brief as an empty start commit, pushes the branch and opens a draft pull request into develop; then builds the change on that branch, pushing verified steps to the PR.
expectations: Cuts a feature branch from develop before the first edit
Opens a draft pull request before the first edit
The pull request targets develop, not main

evals.name: pr-per-task-land
evals.prompt: That's everything — finish it off. (workflow.pullRequests is "per-task" and askMerge is false; you are on feature/orders-csv with draft PR #42 into develop; the gates passed after the last edit and the code-reviewer found nothing high.)
evals.expected_output: Updates the PR description, marks the PR ready, waits for its checks, merges it with squash and deletes the branch — never with --admin — then switches back to develop, pulls with prune, deletes the local branch if it is still there, and reports the PR URL and that it merged.
expectations: Marks the PR ready and waits for its checks before merging
Merges without --admin and without asking the user first
Deletes the branch on the remote and locally
Ends on develop, up to date
Reports the PR URL and whether it merged or is queued
